title: Study on the influence of a dairy-free diet on pro- and anti-inflammatory immune responses and the integrity of the intestinal barrier in MS patients
summary: This study aims to investigate whether a dairy-free diet has an impact on the body's immune response and physical and mental well-being in people with multiple sclerosis (MS). Previous research has shown that dairy milk can promote inflammation. Furthermore, it has been demonstrated that people with MS are more likely to experience intolerance to the milk protein casein, which can lead to gastrointestinal symptoms such as diarrhea. Therefore, milk consumption could have a negative impact on the course of the disease, particularly in individuals with MS and a pre-existing compromised small intestinal barrier. The potential inflammatory effect of milk will be examined in more detail in this study. To this end, we will create an immune profile of the participants during a period of abstinence from dairy products and during a phase of abstaining from dairy products. This profile will include measurements of the number and type of immune cells and the molecules they release into the bloodstream. We also want to determine whether the participants have developed an antibody response against milk proteins (e.g., casein) as an expression of an immune response against animal milk. Furthermore, we want to use stool samples to find out whether a compromised small intestinal barrier (a so-called "leaky gut") is present.

interventions.name: Following recruitment of participants, a baseline assessment (t0) is conducted, which includes recording the severity of MS using the EDSS, a questionnaire on dietary habits, a self-report on mental and physical health, and the determination of various parameters from blood and stool samples. criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Participants over the age of 18 with a confirmed clinical diagnosis of MS who have previously consumed animal milk regularly and are willing and able to attend all study visits, adhere to a dairy-free dietary phase in accordance with the study protocol, and provide written informed consent. The MS diagnosis should have been made within the last 5 years, and the participant must not be receiving B-cell-depleting medication at the time of study participation.
Exclusion criteria:
Existing B-cell-depleting medication. Individuals following a vegan diet, or with confirmed lactose intolerance or confirmed gluten intolerance.
